issues.claim: a few other observations are argued to disagree, but the mainstream view is that gravity travels at light speed
issues.problem: Wikipedia Speed of gravity: the only contested results are the 2002 Kopeikin-Fomalont measurement (reported 0.8 to 1.2 c, consistent with c) and a 2025 paper challenging GW170817. 'Other observations disagree' implies false balance.
issues.fix: A few papers have questioned the result, but general relativity and every precise test say gravity travels at light speed.

issues.claim: Without the Sun, humans would freeze within weeks.
issues.problem: Caltech expert Q&A: the surface falls below freezing in days to about a week, and surface life dies within months to years. 'Humans freeze within weeks' is not directly sourced.
issues.fix: Without the Sun, the surface would drop below freezing within about a week.

issues.claim: a bullet train at one hundred kilometers an hour
issues.problem: Shinkansen operating speeds are 260 to 320 km/h. At 100 km/h the 171-year figure is right, but the vehicle is mislabeled.
issues.fix: For example, imagine a car at one hundred kilometers an hour heading for the Sun.

issues.claim: caught by two detectors called LIGO and Virgo
issues.problem: Wikipedia GW170817: three detectors observed it (two LIGO sites plus Virgo).
issues.fix: One more thing: that neutron star crash was caught by three detectors, two LIGO and one Virgo.

issues.claim: Most people believe we would notice at once
issues.problem: No source for what most people believe.
issues.fix: Many people assume we would notice at once, that the sky would go dark and Earth would fly off instantly.
